title: Global Color Balance
text: Use a restrained whole-room palette. Let large furniture carry the base tones, medium pieces support them, and accessories provide small accents. A practical rule is 60-30-10: about 60 percent calm base colors, 30 percent secondary tones, and 10 percent accent color. Avoid giving every object a different strong color.

title: Global Material Consistency
text: Keep 1 dominant material family and at most 1 or 2 supporting material families in one room. For example: wood + fabric as base, black metal as accent. Avoid mixing too many competing finishes unless the style explicitly allows it.

title: Visual Hierarchy in a Room
text: Choose one main visual anchor per zone. Large furniture such as bed, sofa, desk, or dining table should visually lead the room. Accessories should support the anchor instead of competing with it. Keep tall, dark, or high-contrast pieces limited.

title: Decor Density Control
text: Use decor sparingly. Empty space is part of the design. Prefer a few intentional accessories instead of many small scattered objects. If the room already has strong furniture shapes or strong colors, reduce extra decor.

title: Soft and Hard Balance
text: Balance hard surfaces such as wood, glass, and metal with soft elements such as rug, curtain, cushion, or fabric lampshades. Soft elements reduce visual harshness and help tie the palette together.

title: Bedroom Color Pairing
text: In a bedroom, the bed should be the visual anchor. Keep bed, headboard, and rug in the same tonal family or closely related neutrals. Nightstands and lamps should support the bed, not outshine it. Wardrobes and dressers should usually stay quieter than the bed in both color and texture.

title: Bedroom Lamp Placement
text: Bedside lamps belong visually near the bed, usually on nightstands or visually paired beside it. Use symmetry for calm bedrooms and slight asymmetry for more casual rooms. Do not overload both sides with many decorative objects.

title: Bedroom Soft Layers
text: Use rug, cushions, and throw blanket as the main soft styling tools in a bedroom. Keep cushions and throws within the same palette as the bed, but allow one muted accent tone. Avoid more than one strong accent color on the bed.

title: Living Room Color Pairing
text: In a living room, the sofa is usually the main color anchor. Coffee table, side table, and TV console should support the sofa with complementary neutrals or wood/metal contrast. Accent color should appear through cushions, art, or a small decor item rather than through many large objects.

title: Living Room Decor Placement
text: Place small decor where it supports existing furniture clusters: side table, console table, coffee table, or media shelf. Avoid spreading decor evenly everywhere. A single vase, one plant, or one lamp is often enough per support surface.

title: Living Room Lighting Layers
text: Layer living room lighting. Ceiling light handles general light, while floor lamp or table lamp adds warmth near seating. Place lamps near sofa edges, armchairs, or side tables, not in the center of the room. Lighting should frame the seating group.

title: Studio Unified Palette
text: A studio should use one unified palette across sleeping, working, and living zones. Different zones may vary in texture or accent strength, but not in completely different color families. Use rug, lamp, and decor to suggest zone identity without breaking visual unity.

title: Studio Zone Anchors
text: Let each studio zone have one primary anchor: bed for sleep, desk for work, sofa for lounge. Accessories should stay close to their anchor. Do not let decor from one zone visually spill too much into another.

title: Office Color Pairing
text: In an office, the desk is the main anchor. Keep desk, chair, and storage consistent in tone and material. Use a restrained palette to reduce distraction. Accent color should be small and intentional, such as art, lamp, or a single chair detail.

title: Office Accessory Control
text: Desk accessories should look functional first and decorative second. Prefer monitor, laptop, keyboard, mouse, and one desk lamp as the core set. Avoid adding many small decorative objects on the work surface.

title: Kitchen Color Pairing
text: In a kitchen, cabinets define the main visual field. Keep large cabinet surfaces quiet and cohesive. Countertop appliances should be limited in visible color variety. If cabinets are strong in color, keep small appliances neutral. If cabinets are neutral, one accent appliance is acceptable.

title: Kitchen Countertop Styling
text: Countertop styling should remain sparse. Group functional appliances in one zone instead of scattering them. A small plant or one decorative object may soften the kitchen, but avoid crowding prep surfaces.

title: Anchor Rule for Bed
text: The bed pairs best with mattress, headboard, rug, bedside lamp, cushions, and throw blanket. Keep bedside elements balanced. Rug should visually extend the bed zone rather than compete with it.

title: Anchor Rule for Desk
text: Desk accessories should look orderly and non-overlapping. A monitor or laptop is primary, a desk lamp is secondary. Keep left-right balance and reserve some empty desk surface.

title: Anchor Rule for Side Table
text: A side table usually needs only one main styled item, or two if both are small and visually different, for example lamp plus a small plant. Avoid stacking many decorative pieces on a small table.

title: Anchor Rule for Console Table
text: Console tables work best with a vertical visual partner such as mirror or wall art, plus one small tabletop object. Keep the tabletop composition centered or intentionally asymmetrical, but never crowded.

title: Anchor Rule for Sofa
text: The sofa is styled mainly through cushions, throw blanket, nearby rug, and adjacent lighting. Use cushions to repeat the room palette, not introduce unrelated colors.

title: Anchor Rule for TV Console
text: TV console styling should stay calm. TV is the main visual object. Speakers and small decor should stay secondary and should not create a busy media wall.

title: Wall Decor Composition
text: Wall decor should support furniture below it. Mirror, art, or clock should visually align with the anchor furniture group. Do not scatter many unrelated wall objects across every wall.

title: Window Treatment Styling
text: Curtains and blinds should connect the room palette rather than stand out too much. Use window treatments to soften large walls and reinforce the main palette. They should usually be quieter than the main furniture anchor.

title: Ceiling Lighting Role
text: Ceiling lighting sets the room tone but should not dominate the color story. Pendant lights may act as a focal point over dining or island zones. Track lights and ceiling lights should remain visually coherent with hardware finishes in the room.

title: modern surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For modern interiors, recommended wall base colors: #F4F1EA, #ECE7DE, #E3DDD2. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #D6D0C6, #CFC8BC. Ceiling colors: #FAFAF7. Recommended wood floor tones: #C9A47E, #B88F68, #7D5E47. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #BDB7AE, #A9A39A. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for modern unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

text: In modern, use large_casegoods colors from #F2EEE8, #D8D2C8, #7A5A43, #3C3C3C. Use small_casegoods colors from #F2EEE8, #D8D2C8, #A68563, #2F2F2F. Use upholstery colors from #E8E1D8, #CFC6BB, #AFA79C, #7C858D. Use textile colors from #F3EFE8, #DDD4C8, #C9C2B7, #B7B09F. Use lighting hardware colors from #111111, #5B5B5B, #B8B8B8. title: japandi surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For japandi interiors, recommended wall base colors: #EEE7DD, #E5DDD1, #DCCFBE. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #C8B9A5, #B9A58C. Ceiling colors: #F7F3EC. Recommended wood floor tones: #C79E72, #AE845C, #7B6046. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #B7B0A4, #A39A8D. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for japandi unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: japandi color strategy by role
text: In japandi, use large_casegoods colors from #E9E0D3, #D7C9B8, #9B7F63, #3C342E. Use small_casegoods colors from #E9E0D3, #CDBCA7, #A58263, #2F2A27. Use upholstery colors from #E7DED2, #D5C7B6, #B9AA98, #8D7B67. Use textile colors from #F1EADF, #DDD1C0, #C8B49A, #A38C76. Use lighting hardware colors from #2C2622, #6F6257, #B5A79B. Accent colors must come mainly from #B27F5C, #7E8A72, #8E7760 and should stay limited to small objects or soft accessories. Rule: large furniture should stay neutral or wood-based; accent colors must not dominate wardrobes, desks, beds, sofas, or full walls.

title: scandinavian surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For scandinavian interiors, recommended wall base colors: #F6F4EE, #F0EEE7, #E8E4DB. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #D9D5CC, #CFCABF. Ceiling colors: #FBFBF8. Recommended wood floor tones: #D6B48C, #C89E73, #A97B56. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #C4C1B8, #B0ADA4. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for scandinavian unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: scandinavian color strategy by role
text: In scandinavian, use large_casegoods colors from #F7F4EE, #E6E1D7, #CBAE8B, #6D746F. Use small_casegoods colors from #F7F4EE, #DDD8CE, #BDA07F, #7A8781. Use upholstery colors from #E9E6DE, #D9D6CF, #C1C8C3, #9AA7A2. Use textile colors from #F2EFE8, #E1DDD4, #CBD4D0, #B9C1BC. Use lighting hardware colors from #222222, #7E8683, #CFCFCB. Use appliance visible colors from #E5E5E1, #BFC6C3, #1F1F1F. Use decor colors from #D0B08C, #98ABA8, #889B95, #9E8E78. Accent colors must come mainly from #C8A27A, #7E9A96, #A1B6B0 and should stay limited to small objects or soft accessories. Rule: large furniture should stay neutral or wood-based; accent colors must not dominate wardrobes, desks, beds, sofas, or full walls.

title: industrial surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For industrial interiors, recommended wall base colors: #E3DED5, #D4CEC4, #C4BCB1. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #64615B, #4B4A46. Ceiling colors: #F0EEE9. Recommended wood floor tones: #9A7455, #7F5F46, #5F4737. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #8F8B84, #77736E. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for industrial unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: industrial color strategy by role
text: In industrial, use large_casegoods colors from #6B655D, #A08870, #3B3B39, #B7AA98. Use small_casegoods colors from #7B746B, #B59B81, #222222, #9D9488. Use upholstery colors from #7B7369, #9B8C7B, #545E64, #B9ADA0. Use textile colors from #C9BBAE, #A99B8E, #7B756E, #585752. Use lighting hardware colors from #111111, #3E3E3E, #8C8C8A. Use appliance visible colors from #111111, #6E6E6E, #B7B7B4. Use decor colors from #A67C52, #6E7A74, #8A6B58. Accent colors must come mainly from #A56E43, #6D7A71, #7B8890 and should stay limited to small objects or soft accessories. Rule: large furniture should stay neutral or wood-based; accent colors must not dominate wardrobes, desks, beds, sofas, or full walls.

title: industrial color guidance for large_casegoods
text: For industrial, large storage and main hard furniture such as wardrobe, dresser, desk, cabinet, bookshelf, dining table should prefer colors: #6B655D, #A08870, #3B3B39, #B7AA98. title: classic surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For classic interiors, recommended wall base colors: #F2E9DA, #E9DDCC, #DED0BB. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #C7B299, #B79B7A. Ceiling colors: #FBF7F0. Recommended wood floor tones: #A57952, #855E3E, #65452D. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #C8C0B5, #B2A99E. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for classic unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: classic color strategy by role
text: In classic, use large_casegoods colors from #DCC9AF, #B89772, #6D4D35, #3E2F26. Use small_casegoods colors from #E4D5C2, #C5A787, #7B5B44, #4A3930. Use upholstery colors from #D9CABB, #C7B299, #A98C70, #7E5E4A. Use textile colors from #F0E5D6, #D9C5AE, #C8B299, #A9896A. Use lighting hardware colors from #8C6A43, #B08D57, #3F3127. Use appliance visible colors from #D8D1C7, #A49A8D, #3F3127. Use decor colors from #B88A55, #7F5E45, #A9805B. Accent colors must come mainly from #A66B3D, #8C5C47, #B08D57 and should stay limited to small objects or soft accessories. Rule: large furniture should stay neutral or wood-based; accent colors must not dominate wardrobes, desks, beds, sofas, or full walls.

title: boho surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For boho interiors, recommended wall base colors: #F3E7D8, #E9D9C8, #E0CEB8. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #C98B67, #B96E53. Ceiling colors: #FAF4EC. Recommended wood floor tones: #C28E63, #A77249, #7C573C. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #C7B7A6, #B6A08D. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for boho unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: boho color strategy by role
text: In boho, use large_casegoods colors from #DAB997, #B98A61, #7B5A43, #A57C67. Use small_casegoods colors from #E1C8A9, #C79166, #8C674A, #6A5244. Use upholstery colors from #D8B39A, #C96B4B, #8E8D6B, #A68573. Use textile colors from #E8D2BE, #D8B273, #B96B4B, #8E8D6B. Use lighting hardware colors from #6B503F, #A57C61, #C7A782. Accent colors must come mainly from #C96B4B, #D8B273, #5E7B6E and should stay limited to small objects or soft accessories. Rule: large furniture should stay neutral or wood-based; accent colors must not dominate wardrobes, desks, beds, sofas, or full walls.

title: midcentury surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For midcentury interiors, recommended wall base colors: #F1E8D9, #E7DCCB, #DCCFB8. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #C2A47C, #B58C60. Ceiling colors: #FBF8F2. Recommended wood floor tones: #B17B4F, #8E603D, #6F492F. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #BFB6AA, #AAA094. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for midcentury unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: midcentury color strategy by role
text: In midcentury, use large_casegoods colors from #D7C1A5, #A66C43, #6A4A35, #364B57. Use small_casegoods colors from #E2D0B8, #C77C47, #7A5A45, #4F6D7A. title: wabi_sabi surfaces: wall, floor, ceiling
text: For wabi_sabi interiors, recommended wall base colors: #E9E2D6, #DED4C6, #D2C5B2. Accent wall colors (use sparingly): #B9AA95, #A38D77. Ceiling colors: #F6F1EA. Recommended wood floor tones: #BA916A, #9B7556, #74563F. Recommended stone/concrete floor tones: #B8B0A4, #A39A8F. Rule: walls and floor must stay calmer than the main furniture anchor. Do not use strong saturated wall colors for wabi_sabi unless the room is explicitly designed around a bold feature wall.

title: wabi_sabi color strategy by role
text: In wabi_sabi, use large_casegoods colors from #D8CBB8, #BFAF9A, #8B7E6A, #4B433C. Use small_casegoods colors from #E0D4C3, #C7B5A0, #9C8A74, #5E544B. Use upholstery colors from #D7CCBE, #C1B2A0, #A38D77, #7B7166. Use textile colors from #E7DED3, #D3C6B6, #B8A896, #9B8B7A. Use lighting hardware colors from #4A433D, #877C73, #B9AFA5. Use appliance visible colors from #DED8CF, #AFA79C, #5C554F. Use decor colors from #A38D77, #8B7E6A, #746A60, #B59C84. Accent colors must come mainly from #A38D77, #7B7166, #8E7F70 and should stay limited to small objects or soft accessories. Rule: large furniture should stay neutral or wood-based; accent colors must not dominate wardrobes, desks, beds, sofas, or full walls.

title: modern core styling guidance
text: modern style uses overall palette #E6E1D6, #B9C1C7, #2F3A3F, #C99C6B, #8A8D8F. Preferred materials: glass, metal, neutral fabric. Lighting character: neutral 3000-3500K, clean fixtures. Wall base colors: #F4F1EA, #ECE7DE, #E3DDD2. Wood floor tones: #C9A47E, #B88F68, #7D5E47. Large furniture colors: #F2EEE8, #D8D2C8, #7A5A43, #3C3C3C. Upholstery colors: #E8E1D8, #CFC6BB, #AFA79C, #7C858D. Accent colors for small items only: #B97A56, #7E8C7A, #5F7487. Keep object colors cohesive across the whole room, use large furniture for base tones, and apply accent colors only through small accessories or soft furnishings.
